short: Emperor Valerian was captured alive by the Sasanian king Shapur I, the worst humiliation in Roman history to that point.
full:
In the summer of 260 CE, Emperor Valerian led a Roman army to relieve the besieged city of Edessa in Mesopotamia. Defeated by Shapur I's Sasanian forces and probably weakened by disease, Valerian opened negotiations under a promise of safe conduct; Shapur seized him at the parley instead, together with his staff and much of his army. It was the first and only time a reigning Roman emperor was taken prisoner by a foreign power.

Valerian spent the rest of his life in Persian captivity; hostile Roman writers later claimed he was used as a human footstool and his skin displayed as a trophy after death, though these details are unverifiable. The disaster left the eastern provinces defenceless, prompted Palmyra's rise as their effective guardian, and became the era's starkest symbol of imperial collapse, cited for centuries afterward as Rome's lowest point.
